content.title: Facial Calibration | Isolated Action Units Under a Fixed Identity
content.summary: Lock the character, light and perspective, and only allow partial action units such as eyelids, eyebrows, jaws, line of sight and lip shape to change in stages; use micro resets in the middle to prevent expressions from being mixed into a continuous performance, and tighten the scenes at the end to check that the identity and details are still stable.

quick_start.input_format: Single stable portrait + fixed light background perspective + at least 4 groups of separated facial movements + 1 minor reset + close-up view of rear details
quick_start.recommended_input: The young ceramic courier maintains the same identity and frontal camera position in the cold medical booth, showing one-sided smile, eyes closed, eyebrow raised, side view and rounded lips in sequence; briefly returning to neutral in the middle, and finally advancing to a close-up view of the mask seal.
required_anchors: Lock one face, background, lighting direction and camera axis before any expression change.
Separate the expression into readable local units rather than morphing the whole face continuously.
Keep head motion subordinate to eye, brow, mouth and cheek evidence.
Use a late closer crop only after identity has been repeatedly proven.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Lock the character, light and perspective, and only allow partial action units such as eyelids, eyebrows, jaws, line of sight and lip shape to change in stages; use micro resets in the middle to prevent expressions from being mixed into a continuous performance, and tighten the scenes at the end to check that the identity and details are still stable.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: A facial calibration sequence becomes reusable when identity, lighting, background and camera axis stay fixed while distinct facial action units change one group at a time. Brief micro-resets preserve comparability, and a late controlled crop can test fine identity stability without turning the sequence into a narrative performance.

invariants.rule: Lock one face, background, lighting direction and camera axis before any expression change.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing the portrait setup makes action units impossible to compare.

invariants.rule: Separate the expression into readable local units rather than morphing the whole face continuously.
invariants.purpose: Makes each change diagnosable and reusable.
invariants.ablation_failure: A blended emotional performance hides which feature changed.

invariants.rule: Insert at least one partial reset toward the baseline between larger changes.
invariants.purpose: Prevents accumulated distortion and preserves identity.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a reset, changes can drift into a different face.

invariants.rule: Keep head motion subordinate to eye, brow, mouth and cheek evidence.
invariants.purpose: Maintains a stable portrait while allowing orientation tests.
invariants.ablation_failure: Large head turns replace facial proof with pose variation.

invariants.rule: Use a late closer crop only after identity has been repeatedly proven.
invariants.purpose: Tests detail stability and provides a clear endpoint.
invariants.ablation_failure: Opening in extreme close-up removes the identity baseline.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

instantiations.concept: A young ceramic courier in a cool medical kiosk performs a nonverbal visor-fit calibration: neutral baseline, one-sided brow lift, isolated lower-eyelid tension, closed-lip jaw shift, then one nostril-and-cheek action. A brief neutral reset separates the tests, and the only late close crop verifies the unchanged eye-corner and temple visor seam.

instantiations.concept: A handcrafted wooden puppet in a sunlit rehearsal booth tests five mechanical face controls in a new order: left brow plate, paired eye shutters, closed jaw sliding sideways, one cheek lever, then a full neutral reset. The camera ends on the unchanged eye hinge and wood grain, never on the mouth.
